text:
morgan: Heads up — rolling metrics show a sudden p99 latency jump on the v8 rollout started ~10:30UTC. Hostgroup A affected, p99 doubled. Not a full outage but user-facing slowdowns.

alex: seeing it too. traces show more kernel fallbacks and a lot more frequent small-batch dispatches.

perf-bot: perf-alert: hostgroup-A p50=120ms p95=420ms p99=980ms (+2x) since 1975123400. KV cache hit rate down 18%.

jamal: timeline: v8 pushed -> tokenizer changed subtoken rules -> immediate shift in sequence length distribution (median seq ~ 24 -> 38). That matches increased batching churn.

morgan: exact symptom I'm worried about: runtime is switching to a slower kernel for many requests instead of the optimized fp16 kernel. kernel-selection log shows lots of misroute events.

alex: here's an excerpt from the agent logs (redacted):
```
[1975123462] kernel_select: requested fp16_fast, selected fp32_fallback (reason: seqlen_bin_overflow)
[1975123462] batcher: dispatched batch_size=2 latency_expect=8ms
[1975123463] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.62 -> 0.50 (evicts++)
```

lin: interesting — batcher heuristics throttle window was tuned for median 20 tokens. If median jumped to ~40, the batching grace timer could prematurely flush batches, causing many tiny batches and mis-selecting kernels tuned for shorter sequences.

taylor: also seeing memory pressure on several GPUs around the same time; noisy-tenant on the same host used burst mode -> prefetch/evict threshold triggered. That would reduce KV cache benefits.

jamal: I ran a short perf profile on one affected host. Key points: kernel selection path checks sequence length then estimated workspace bytes. Because the tokenizer now yields longer tail, our kernel-choice comparator miscalculates workspace due to an old stride assumption.

alex: can you paste the profiler opcounts?

jamal: sure, minimal snippet:
```
opcounts: conv=12k attn=4300 gemm=7900 workspace_est=1.3GB actual_workspace=1.6GB
kernel_pick_score(fp16_fast)=-1.4  // negative => reject
```

morgan: so fp16_fast rejected due to underestimated workspace -> selects fp32_fallback which is slower and uses more memory -> cascading evictions and latency.

lin: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) rollback v8 tokenizer for the hosted route, 2) force kernel-selection policy to allow fp16_fast for seqlen<128 unless workspace blows up, 3) increase batcher grace timer by 5ms for hostgroup-A.

taylor: I'd add: pin noisy tenant to lower priority on those GPUs and disable background prefetch bursts for 30m.

alex: we should gather a small reproducer: send mixed seq-len samples matching v8 distribution to a canary and run with increased tracing to confirm workspace mis-estimate. jamal can you run perf_collect.sh on canary?

jamal: running now on canary-3:
```
./perf_collect.sh --host canary-3 --duration 300 --kernels=all --trace=kernel_select,kv_cache,batcher
```

perf-bot: note: opened incident ticket INF-2026-213 with initial metrics link https://perf.local/INF-2026-213

morgan: OK operational plan: 1) throttle noisy tenant (taylor), 2) run reproducer (jamal), 3) deploy kernel-selection temporary relax (alex), 4) rollback tokenizer if p99 doesn't drop within 15m (morgan).

lin: small code change to try — in kernel_selector.cpp change seqlen_bin overflow check to use 1.15x workspace_est multiplier while we investigate. I'll prepare a canary patch.

taylor: throttling noisy tenant now (ID: tenant-873) :locked:  

jamal: reproducer results: confirmed workspace underestimates ~20% for v8 tokenization patterns. After forcing fp16_fast, p99 dropped ~35% on canary. KV hit rate also improved.

alex: patch ready and pushed to canary (kernel-selector: use 1.15 multiplier). Monitoring metrics now.

perf-bot: canary update: p99 down 30% on canary-3, KV hit +8%, kernel fallbacks -64%.

morgan: good. Hold off on full rollout until we have root cause fix — either update the workspace estimator to use actual subtoken-length distribution or add a tokenizer compatibility shim.

lin: created follow-up GH issue: runtime#4821 with reproduction, profile dump, and suggested estimator fix.

taylor: reverting prefetch bursts for the noisy tenant back to normal after 25m window. GPU pressure eased.

morgan: summary: regression traced to v8 tokenizer changing seq-len distribution which exposed a workspace estimation bug in kernel selection, compounded by noisy-tenant-induced memory pressure and a batcher grace timer tuned too low. Mitigation: canary patch to relax kernel-selection threshold deployed; follow-up fix in runtime#4821; rollback path available if metrics worsen.

alex: thumbs up. I'll schedule a postmortem doc and perf regression test to add to CI that uses v8 tokenization samples. :thumbsup:

morgan: thanks all — keep monitoring INF-2026-213 link and update when stable.
